title: Minimax Welfare Regret for Budget-Safe Two-Stage Regimes without Common Overlap
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below the field floor (paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4; salvageable false): the unrestricted sharp regret frontier remains open, while the logarithmic bracket and matched strong-overlap branch are sound.
gap_reasons: The unrestricted three-regime minimax frontier is not determined: the proved lower rate is (nq)^(-1/2), while the observable upper bound retains a square-root logarithmic factor, leaving oeq:sharp-frontier and oeq:continuous-optimism-or-obstruction open.
The strong-overlap result is matched only when kappa^2 is at least q; its q-dominated branch inherits the same unresolved gap.
The repeated description of the learners as ‘exactly safe’ overstates the theorems, which guarantee exact budget compliance only on an event of probability at least 0.95 rather than almost surely.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established an observable finite-grid learner with a logarithmic upper bound, an active-budget rare-path lower bound, and a matched strong-overlap q–kappa branch. The unrestricted rates still differ by a square-root logarithm; neither the continuous-mixture optimism inequality nor a same-model logarithmic obstruction was proved. D0.5 math review passed, but the tier reviewer judged the delivered package subfield below the field floor.
tldr: The project fixes a public menu of three two-stage regimes, including a known zero-cost fallback, and asks for the minimax welfare regret of learners that meet the true budget with probability at least \(0.9\). One oracle-selected optimal feasible ex-ante mixture satisfies a raw trajectory likelihood-ratio \(L^2\) condition, while inferior regimes need no common overlap floor. On the unrestricted class, an observable logarithmically smoothed grid learner and a binding-cost rare-path pair give the bracket \(\min\{1,(nq)^{-1/2}\}\lesssim\mathfrak R_n(q)\lesssim\min\{1,\sqrt{\log(2+nq)/(nq)}\}\). On the strong-overlap restriction, a same-class active-budget pair and a coordinatewise exactly safe learner expose the sharper \(q\)--\(\kappa\) elbow: the rate is matched at \(\min\{1,(\kappa\sqrt n)^{-1}\}\) whenever \(\kappa^2\ge q\), while the \(q\)-dominated branch retains at most the displayed logarithmic residual. Removing or forcing that residual remains the open kernel.
gap: Existing weak-overlap policy learners treat static unconstrained choice and retain policy-class complexity; dynamic budget rules use strong stagewise overlap or control budget excess rather than uniform true-budget safety. Existing constrained offline reinforcement learning assumes bounded occupancy ratios and critic realizability.
fill: The project establishes an observable safe upper bound and an active-budget all-learner converse under raw \(L^2\) coverage of one oracle-selected mixture, then isolates the continuous-simplex inequality or causal obstruction required to determine the exact frontier.
